plan.topic: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: the first Phase 3 diabetes trial, TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (537 adults whose type 2 diabetes was managed with diet and exercise, 40 weeks, vs placebo, The Lancet)
plan.angle: Retatrutide in type 2 diabetes: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 (The Lancet, 2026), 40 weeks vs placebo, adults whose type 2 diabetes wasn't controlled with diet and exercise alone. One weight number for the top dose vs placebo with per-arm n and the named estimand, then one HbA1c line with its arm and the placebo figure. Placebo-controlled only, no tirzepatide arm. Status, credited to Lilly with a date: investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, and a plan to file isn't approval. One GI line. No online products. Ask a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. Prescriber line. CTA to 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' only if that video is published and says the comparison is indirect; otherwise 'follow for more'.

plan.why: Spin-off of yesterday's live retatrutide long-form, sending traffic to it. It's a new trial we haven't covered, and retatrutide searches are up (radar momentum 80). | fact-check: Confirmed: TRANSCEND-T2D-1 was a 40-week, randomized, double-blind trial of retatrutide vs placebo in 537 adults whose type 2 diabetes was inadequately controlled with diet and exercise (HbA1c 7.0–9.5%, BMI ≥23), published in The Lancet and presented at ADA in June 2026. Reported weight change: 4 mg −11.5%, 9 mg −13.9%, 12 mg −15.3%, placebo −2.6%. Lilly also reported −16.8% for 12 mg under a different estimand, and the two get mixed up. The script must name the estimand next to the number it uses and use per-arm n from the Lancet paper, not 537. Status: Lilly said (Jul 2026) it plans to submit to the FDA in Q1 2027. The status line must be credited to a Lilly statement dated at or near that date, not to the June trial paper. Population wording: 'type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise alone, not well controlled'. These were not people with obesity specifically (BMI ≥23). CTA problem: the playbook says 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' uses a frame with no randomized head-to-head trial behind it, and this Short states correctly that there was no tirzepatide arm. Funnelling viewers into a 'beat' title right after saying so is contradictory. Point the CTA there only if that video is published and clearly calls its comparison indirect. Otherwise use 'follow for more' and a related-video link to another published retatrutide long-form. This is a single-drug Short in the weak 20:00 slot, which is acceptable as a test.

package.title: Retatrutide and Type 2 Diabetes: First Phase 3 Results #shorts
package.description:
Retatrutide's first Phase 3 type 2 diabetes trial (TRANSCEND-T2D-1: 537 adults not well controlled with diet and exercise alone, 40 weeks) found every dose cut A1C more than placebo; side effects were mostly gastrointestinal, like nausea, generally mild to moderate.
It's investigational, not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026. In August 2026, Lilly said it plans to file in the first quarter of 2027 for obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain, not diabetes, and a plan to file isn't approval.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number in this Short against the trial registry, a published summary of the Lancet paper and Lilly's own releases, and they're all correct. TRANSCEND-T2D-1 was a phase 3, double-blind, placebo-only trial. It ran 40 weeks in 537 adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled by diet and exercise alone, split 1:1:1:1 across retatrutide 4, 9 and 12 mg or placebo. A1C (the 3-month blood sugar average) was the main goal, and every dose lowered it more than placebo did (1.69%, 1.86% and 1.94% vs 0.81%). Weight fell 15.3% on 12 mg vs 2.6% on placebo. The most common side effects were stomach and gut related, generally mild to moderate. Lilly's 5 August 2026 Q2 release says it plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027 for obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain, and diabetes isn't listed. The script says there's no tirzepatide group, gives a dated "not FDA-approved" status with "a plan to file isn't approval", includes the don't-switch line, and sends viewers to a prescriber about approved options or trials. The title's question is answered by about 15 s. A few small wording and source-list fixes are below.

issues.problem: The trial randomised people 1:1:1:1, but 537 can't be split into four exactly equal groups. The script also never gives the size of each group, which our number rules require.
issues.fix: Narration: "40 weeks. 537 adults whose type 2 diabetes wasn't well controlled with diet and exercise alone were randomly split evenly, about 134 per group: three retatrutide doses or placebo." On screen: "537 adults, about 134 per group, 40 weeks"

issues.claim: for obesity, sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain, not type 2 diabetes
issues.problem: Lilly names obstructive sleep apnea, and it doesn't say 'not type 2 diabetes'. Diabetes simply isn't on its list. Our wording should stay within what the source says.
issues.fix: "In August, Lilly said it plans to file with the FDA in the first quarter of 2027 for obesity, obstructive sleep apnea and knee osteoarthritis pain. Type 2 diabetes wasn't on that list. And a plan to file isn't approval."

issues.claim: Lilly (Aug 2026): plans to file Q1 2027 for obesity, not diabetes
issues.problem: Leaves out two of the three conditions Lilly named, and says 'not diabetes' when Lilly only left it off the list.
issues.fix: "Lilly (Aug 2026): plans to file Q1 2027 for obesity, sleep apnea, knee pain. Diabetes not listed"

issues.claim: Side effects: mostly gastrointestinal, like nausea.
issues.problem: Accurate, but it drops the source's qualifier that these were generally mild to moderate and eased over time.
issues.fix: "Catch: there's no tirzepatide group. Side effects: mostly gastrointestinal, like nausea, generally mild to moderate."

issues.problem: The NIDDK page says it was last reviewed April 2018.
issues.fix: Set year to "2018" and publisher to "NIDDK (NIH), last reviewed April 2018".

issues.problem: No scene cites it. It covers the March 2026 topline results and reports a different weight figure from another analysis (16.8%), so it could cause confusion further down the pipeline.
